name: Black Coral
lede: Black Coral is a Crayola-list name for a dark bluish grey; the swatch looks nothing like black, and the books say little about the name itself.

sections.title: A name from the sea
sections.body:
The name pairs [[black]] with [[coral]], and it appears in the Wikipedia list of Crayola colors [1]. The swatch is a dark, slightly blue grey, with the nearest ISCC-NBS name "grayish blue" at a distance of 3.2 [1]. It sits near [[slate-grey]] and [[charcoal]] more than anything pink or red.

Black coral itself is a real material. In Finlay's list of gem materials found naturally in each US state, Hawaii is paired with black coral [2]. The books we read give no history for the color name, so none is claimed here.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch appears in 425 of our 23,781 paintings, 1.79 percent, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, found in 38 of the 1,674 paintings from that century, 2.7 times the expected rate against the same museums' baseline [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a mid-tone [3].
